# chroordinate <a href="https://joe-m-shaw.github.io/chroordinate/"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="250" alt="chroordinate website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/joe-m-shaw/chroordinate/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/joe-m-shaw/chroordinate)
<!-- badges: end -->

chroordinate allows you to coordinate chromosome coordinates during data analysis.

## Installation

You can install the development version of chroordinate from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("joe-m-shaw/chroordinate")
```

## Usage

`chroordinate` makes it easier to work with chromosome coordinates during data
analysis. For example, in cases where multiple descriptions of chromosome
coordinates are included in the same column, the `mutate_coordinates` function
extracts the coordinates into two separate columns.

```{r, echo = FALSE}

test_df <- tibble::tribble(
  ~"gene", ~"variant", ~"region",
  "GENE1", "SNV", "12345",
  "GENE1", "CNV", "12345..12348",
  "GENE1", "Indel", "12345^23456")

knitr::kable(test_df)

```

```{r, include = TRUE}

test_df |> 
  chroordinate::mutate_coordinates(region)

```

## Naming convention

In `chroordinate` chromosomes are referred to as "chromosome" for clarity, instead
of "chr" (which can be mistaken for meaning "character") or "chrom".
For the second coordinate in a location, `chroordinate` uses "end" not "stop".

## Logo

The `chroordinate` logo uses an icon from FlatIcon made by [Magnific](https://www.flaticon.com/free-icon/genetics_5685648?term=chromosome&related_id=5685648).
